reason: H0 only formats compiler errors individually through the single-Error overload with default formatting options. It does not directly fuzz the new ErrorList overload, multi-error aggregation, or the _colored and _withErrorIds configurations used by the expanded formatter API. Although H0 can reach CompilerStack::generateIR through setViaIR(), the new aggregate-formatting call is gated on parseAndAnalyze() rejecting compiler-generated IR, so ordinary compilation does not exercise its list-formatting semantics.
evidence: S1 adds SourceReferenceFormatter::formatErrorInformation(langutil::ErrorList const& _errors, CharStreamProvider const& _charStreamProvider, bool _colored, bool _withErrorIds).
S1 expands the single-Error formatErrorInformation overload with _colored and _withErrorIds and constructs SourceReferenceFormatter directly.
H0 calls SourceReferenceFormatter::formatErrorInformation(*error, m_compiler) and supplies neither an ErrorList nor either boolean configuration.
CompilerStack::generateIR calls formatErrorInformation(stack.errors(), stack) only in the solAssert failure message associated with !yulAnalysisSuccessful.

H0 enables the IR route with m_compiler.setViaIR(m_compilerInput.viaIR), but contains no direct construction of ErrorList, formatter configuration, or controlled CharStreamProvider/source-reference combinations.
recommended_action: Add a focused formatter fuzz target that generates ErrorList collections with varied error types, severities, source references, and associated character streams, and exercises all _colored/_withErrorIds combinations. Retain the compiler harness for end-to-end coverage of CompilerStack::generateIR.
